en: , my master...
note: Fragment after the name (servant mode), as M0#0/M1#633; used by Jeremy, Oliver, Matthew, Stanley, Wayne and more; the next row starts a new sentence. Variants: Kurt the tobacconist greeting a customer (87118/87687) and Clio in love (402261/402743) are not servants

en: My lord and master... Your orders...
My body's my bread and butter, and my joints ache.
Am I getting old already...? Drives me nuts.
I'll always obey you, Master...
Feels like I didn't sleep a wink. I'm beat...
Don't tell me I've been sleepwalking...
What on earth are you doing?
Whoa, whoa there! Er, afternoon.
Setting up for today's street show. Heh heh...
I'm Jeremy. Putting on a show's my job.
And getting yelled at by coppers is, too.
note: 'is (my job), too': follows #10 'Putting on a show's my job.' (msg 684) and #108 (msg 1373, slice 001), which must also end with '... my job.'

en: Seems doing tricks in the street's a no-no.
Ha, to hell with 'em! Watch my act and laugh!
What an odd fellow...
Whoa, whoa! 'Odd fellow,' and that's it?!
Come and watch later, too, all right?
You'll see a knife-throwing act full of thrills!
Nope, nope! I told you, I'm still setting up.
Hey there,
, my good sir!
While you're in London, don't you miss
my act, or you'll be sorry!
And tips are always welcome, any time!
Hiya,
We keep running into each other! Isn't this
what they call a fated meeting, eh?
Ah, never mind, don't answer. Even I think
that joke was creepy. Sorry, sorry, ha ha!
Hey. You look worn out, mate.
Me too. I'm packing it in for today.
Come to the main street by day for my act.
So you're a street performer...
That's right. Well, I'm off home. See ya.
Wanna see me in all my glory? Come by day!
Follow me all you like, I've got no secret hideout.
It's me, Jeremy, see?
Nice night, eh? Makes a fella want to brood.
Heh, guess that's not really my style, huh?
Nice night, eh? You doing all right?
Say, you've got something on your mind, don't you?
<Something like that...>
note: Answer choice (no used_in), stern player; leads to msg 919

en: <Mind your own business>
note: Answer choice (no used_in); leads to msg 937

en: Thought so. See, I meet all kinds of people,
so I can kind of tell, you know?
note: Ends a sentence: followed by #46 (msg 919) and #126 (msg 1628)

en: So even a guy like you has worries, huh.
Oh, is that so? Then that grim
face of yours must be how you were born.
note: Continues #47 (msg 937); msg 1648 starts with this row, see report

en: A good belly laugh helps now and then, eh?
Fretting over a total stranger? What an odd one.
Isn't that just normal? Caring doesn't cost
a penny, after all! Heh heh heh...
Roll up! Ladies, gents, boys and girls,
come and see! I, Jeremy, bring you all
a street show full of thrills and laughs!
If you like it, drop a heartfelt tip
in the tin here with a clink!
Or a rustle of banknotes, that's fine, too!
(Hmm, quite nimble. As a servant, he
might prove useful...)
Oh! Who's that I see? The gent from before!
You came to see me in all my glory!
Ooh! All right, today I'm going all out!
Ha ha, you like my act that much?
Now then, behold these blazing sticks!
Watch London's finest juggler, Jeremy,
toss them around as he pleases!
Oh,
Back again, are you?
Love a show, eh? You must have time to kill.
Well, whatever. Customers are always welcome.
Hey.
Say what you like, you sure come by a lot.
I hear you've been walking all over town.
<It's part of my work>
note: Answer choice (no used_in); leads to msg 1163

en: <Don't pry>
Ooh, a detective or something? How dashing.
Unlike me, you're the brainy type, ha ha.
